name: tidy-formatter
description: Format & beautify JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX/TSX, CSS, SCSS, LESS, HTML & JSON. A safe, config-respecting replacement for JS-CSS-HTML Formatter that never touches your files unless you ask.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Tidy Formatter
walkthroughs.description: Set up safe, consent-first formatting: opt in when you want, migrate from JS-CSS-HTML Formatter, and keep full control of format-on-save.

steps.title: Safety first
steps.description: Tidy never writes a file that fails an equivalence check against your original. When it cannot prove the output equivalent, it makes zero edits and your file is left byte-identical.

steps.title: Try it now
steps.description:
See Tidy work in 30 seconds, on scratch buffers that never touch your disk.
[Open the playground](command:tidy.openPlayground)
Then run [Tidy: Preview Format (Diff)](command:tidy.previewFormat) on the playground tab to see a read-only diff of exactly what Tidy would change.

steps.title: Use Tidy as your formatter
steps.description: Run [Tidy: Use Tidy as My Formatter](command:tidy.useAsFormatter) to opt in per language: fully reversible, nothing is written until you confirm.

steps.title: Format on save: your choice
steps.description: Tidy never hooks the save event. Want format on save? The opt-in command can write $(gear) editor.formatOnSave for the exact languages you confirm, with one-click revert, or you set it yourself.

steps.title: Migrating from JS-CSS-HTML Formatter
steps.description: Run [Tidy: Migrate from JS-CSS-HTML Formatter](command:tidy.runMigration) to import your JS-CSS-HTML Formatter settings (its .vscode/formatter.json) and switch over safely.

tidy.maxFileSizeKB.description: Skip formatting (with a notification) for documents larger than this size in KB. 0 disables the size guard. For JSON and JSONC documents, tidy.json.maxFileSizeKB takes precedence over this value.
tidy.maxFileSizeKB.markdownDescription:

Docs: [Key settings](https://github.com/ced-lab-gh/tidy-formatter#key-settings).

tidy.json.maxFileSizeKB.description: Size cap in KB for JSON and JSONC documents only, taking precedence over tidy.maxFileSizeKB for these two languages. JSON gets a higher default because Tidy formats it on a fast linear path and verifies it with a cheap value-equality check, so large files such as package-lock.json format instead of being skipped. 0 disables the cap for JSON/JSONC. When this setting is unset, an explicitly configured tidy.maxFileSizeKB still applies to JSON.

tidy.wrap_line_length.description: Maximum characters per line before wrapping; 0 disables wrapping. Used for HTML and JavaScript (js-beautify wrap_line_length) and, as the print width, for TypeScript, TSX and JSX (Prettier). It has no effect on JSON, and js-beautify does not wrap CSS, SCSS or LESS by width. For the Prettier languages an unset value keeps Prettier's default of 80. It shares one value with tidy.prettier.printWidth: whichever is set in the higher layer wins.

items.patternErrorMessage: A tag name: a letter, then letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.

tidy.content_unformatted.description: Extra HTML tag names whose content is left exactly as written, for example ["code", "my-snippet"] (js-beautify content_unformatted). They are added to the tags that are always preserved (pre, textarea, xmp, listing, plaintext), which stay whatever you write. Tag names only: letters, digits, hyphens and underscores. Invalid entries are ignored and listed in Show Effective Configuration.

tidy.void_elements.description: Extra HTML tag names printed as void elements, like br and img: tags that never have a closing tag, for example ["my-icon"] (js-beautify void_elements). They are added to the standard HTML void elements, which always stay. Tag names only: letters, digits, hyphens and underscores; elements whose text must stay as written (pre, textarea, xmp, listing, plaintext, script, style) are refused. Invalid entries are ignored and listed in Show Effective Configuration.

tidy.prettier.respectProjectConfig.description: Read the project's Prettier config (.prettierrc, .prettierrc.json/.json5/.yaml/.yml/.toml, or the "prettier" key in package.json) as a data-only layer for the files Prettier prints (TypeScript, TSX, JSX, and a plain .js file that turns out to contain JSX), layered between .editorconfig and .soukformatrc. Only AST-safe stylistic keys are honoured; .prettierrc.js and other code-based configs are never executed. Always ignored in Restricted Mode.

Read the project's Prettier config (.prettierrc, .prettierrc.json/.json5/.yaml/.yml/.toml, or the "prettier" key in package.json) as a data-only layer for the files Prettier prints (TypeScript, TSX, JSX, and a plain .js file that turns out to contain JSX), layered between .editorconfig and .soukformatrc. tidy.soukformatrc.description: Read the project's .soukformatrc file (JSONC) for per-language formatting options and glob overrides, layered above .editorconfig. Disable to ignore .soukformatrc entirely. A workspace .soukformatrc is always ignored in Restricted Mode.
tidy.soukformatrc.markdownDescription:

enumDescriptions: Show a one-time notification when this workspace already configures another formatter or fixer (Prettier, Biome, dprint, ESLint). Tidy never takes over; your default formatter is unchanged.

tidy.statusBar.enable.markdownDescription:
Show the Tidy status bar item: the passive state of the active file plus a short transient result after each format attempt. Purely observational; disabling it changes no formatting behavior.

Docs: [Key settings](https://github.com/ced-lab-gh/tidy-formatter#key-settings).

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run compile && npm run check:chunks
